title: Flat for eight years while the rival tripled
label: The numbers
lede: Circuit City’s sales in fiscal 2008 were about where they had been in fiscal 2000. Over the same years Best Buy more than tripled. The store count kept rising until the final year.

blocks.title: Superstores open at fiscal year end, 1990 to the end
blocks.subtitle: Circuit City superstores only. Fiscal years end on the last day of February.

points.title: CarMax starts
points.text: The first CarMax opened in Richmond in 1993, while the electronics chain was adding about 35 superstores a year.[^8][^6]

points.title: Peak profit, and the appliance exit
points.text: Fiscal 2000 earnings from continuing operations were $271M. That July the company quit major appliances.[^2][^5]

points.title: Commissions end
points.text: The sales force went to hourly pay in February 2003. The store count dipped the next year.[^3][^1]

points.title: 3,400 dismissed
points.text: The wage management initiative of March 28, 2007, a month after fiscal 2007 closed.[^10]

points.title: Most stores ever
points.text: 682 superstores at February 29, 2008, after 43 openings in a year that lost $319.9M.[^1]

points.title: 155 closed, 567 left
points.text: The stores remaining at December 31, 2008, all liquidated by March 8, 2009.[^15][^17]

blocks.source: Store-mix tables in the 10-Ks for fiscal 1994, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2003 and 2008[^8][^7][^6][^4][^3][^1]. Fiscal 1996 (378) is the derived sum of the four superstore formats in the fiscal 1998 table. December 2008 is the domestic store count in the liquidation release[^15]. Mall-based Express stores are excluded.

The stock traded between $23.00 and $31.54 in the first quarter of fiscal 2007 and as low as $5.35 in the third quarter of fiscal 2008.[^1] Blockbuster’s offer in April 2008 was “at least $6.00” a share.[^20] The liquidation release said the company did not expect any value to remain for common shareholders.[^15]
